summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of recurrent infections was readmitted due to positive blood cultures showing gram-positive cocci in clusters, later identified as coagulase-negative staphylococcus. She was started on IV vancomycin, and the PICC line was removed and replaced. Her acute kidney injury improved with hydration, and liver enzyme elevations were attributed to recent antibiotic and statin use, leading to discontinuation of simvastatin. Hepatology recommended follow-up for liver evaluation. She completed a course of antibiotics, remained on oral vancomycin for C. difficile, and was discharged home with nursing services after four days, with plans for outpatient follow-up in infectious disease and hepatology clinics.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
